clue.text: South Park's leading character properly animated

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south

indicators.note: the leading character of a word is its opening letter, so only the front of Park's is wanted

parts.note: the first letter of Park
properly and rightly both mean correctly

explanation.surface: A cartoon character from the TV show South Park is described as being nicely animated.
explanation.walkthrough: South Park looks like one name, the cartoon, but South and Park's leading character are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprightly describes someone lively and full of energy, a close synonym of animated.

clue.text: Having great inclination to soak

definitions.meaning: second meaning: to immerse in liquid

explanation.walkthrough: Inclination sounds like a strong desire, but it is a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: A steep hill has a sharp gradient, and to steep tea is to let it soak in water.

clue.text: One drunk is concerning a flyer after takeoff?

parts.note: re means concerning, as in a letter heading
taken as written

indicators.note: an aircraft after takeoff turns about from the runway, taken here as the name being flipped round

parts.note: El Al is the Israeli national airline

explanation.surface: A drunk is talking about an air passenger after the plane leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: One drunk means one thing that gets drunk, not a drunkard. The reversal signal is loose; the blogger suggested it works better as a general shake-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Real ale is traditional cask beer, something one drinks.

clue.text: Complaint of old lady needing to inhale oxygen

indicators.note: to inhale is to draw in, so the outer word takes the letter inside it

parts.note: an old lady may be a gran, a grandmother
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: An elderly woman grumbling that she needs her oxygen.
explanation.definitionFit: A groan is a moan of discontent, so a complaint.

clue.text: Forbidden steak occasionally, signalled displeasure

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of steak
an audience that booed signalled displeasure

explanation.surface: A diner refused steak and made a fuss about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tabooed is banned by custom, so forbidden.

clue.text: Loudly express desire to tour round in the buff

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go all round it, so the words surround the letter

parts.note: to yell is to shout
a wish is a desire
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: Someone longs to shout about touring the place naked.
explanation.walkthrough: In the buff suggests nakedness; here buff is the pale brownish-yellow colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Buff is a pale yellowish-brown colour, so something in the buff is yellowish.

clue.text: Bag a bed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a large bag of coarse cloth
second meaning: informal word for bed, as in hitting the hay

explanation.surface: Someone instructed to grab a bed, as at a hostel.
explanation.definitionFit: A sack is a coarse bag, and colloquially 'the sack' is one's bed, as in going to the sack to sleep.

clue.text: Sound from brakes perhaps a sort of owl

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a shrill noise as of brakes slammed on
second meaning: a kind of owl, named for its call

explanation.surface: A noise from a car's brakes that might be mistaken for an owl.
explanation.definitionFit: Brakes make a shrill cry when slammed on, and the screech owl is a species named for its call.

clue.text: Companion has no time for book opening

indicators.note: having no time means that letter is taken out

parts.note: the opening of a book is its first chapter
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A busy companion has no time to start reading a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperone accompanies a young person for propriety, so is a companion.

clue.text: The sacrifice of the mass?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a great public sacrifice, originally of a hundred oxen
second meaning: a great number or mass of victims or things

explanation.surface: A churchgoer muses on the sacrifice at the heart of the Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mass suggests church liturgy, but here mass means a huge number; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A hecatomb was an ancient Greek offering of many cattle, and the word came to mean any large-scale slaughter or multitude.

clue.text: Rope's end pulled back arresting a run

indicators.note: something pulled back is drawn in the opposite direction, so the word is read from right to left
to arrest is to seize and hold, so the outer word holds the inner letters

parts.note: the tail is the end of something
taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A rope end is hauled back to stop something running loose.
explanation.walkthrough: TAIL turned round gives LIAT, and A plus R sits inside it after the L.
explanation.definitionFit: A lariat is a lasso, a long rope with a running noose used by cowboys.

clue.text: Odds on bad weather? That's a wrench

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the betting odds on a horse when a race begins
rain is a kind of bad weather

explanation.surface: A punter's view on bookies' odds for rain, followed by a groan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odds on' looks like the betting phrase meaning likely; here 'on' just places one piece before the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrench is a violent twist of a joint, which is what a sprain is.

clue.text: Precariously balanced, title finally is between the same three sides

indicators.note: a letter that is between others is placed inside them

parts.note: in cricket the on side and the leg side are the same half of the field, so ON, ON and LEG name one side three times

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

parts.note: the last letter of title

explanation.surface: Someone describing a precarious stance and a title wedged between three matching sides.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the half of the field behind the batsman's legs is called both the on side and the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing on one leg is the image of being unsteady, an idiom for a precarious balance.

clue.text: Like a bone? Please help yourself

parts.note: O is the exclamation of pleading, as in 'O, please'
to help yourself to something is to take it, steal it

explanation.surface: A host offering a bone to a guest, or a dog, and inviting them to take it.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads as an invitation to theft: 'O, steal!'
explanation.definitionFit: Osteal is the technical adjective for something bony or relating to bone tissue.

clue.text: Son champing to leave hospital department, firm being agreeable

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son

indicators.note: when something leaves a word it is taken out of it

parts.note: champing at the bit means eager and restless
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
Co is short for company

explanation.surface: A son keen to leave a hospital department for a pleasant company.
explanation.definitionFit: Simpatico is borrowed from Italian and Spanish for a likeable, congenial person.

clue.text: Not bound to negotiate lease blockhead is holding up

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the word reads from bottom to top
the word that is holding something has it inside

parts.note: a blockhead is a fool

indicators.note: to negotiate terms is to work them over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of lease rearranged

explanation.surface: A tenant not bound to a lease is being held up by an idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: Bound suggests a contract, but it is a book's binding.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose-leaf pages are held in a ring binder rather than bound into a book.

clue.text: Len, 8, accepted by teacher

indicators.note: something accepted by another is taken in by it, so the second word wraps the first

parts.note: a don is a university teacher
the numeral spelt out

explanation.surface: Someone named Len gets a mark of eight from a teacher.
explanation.walkthrough: 8 looks like a reference to 8-across, but it is simply the number. Len Deighton is the British spy novelist who wrote The IPCRESS File.
explanation.definitionFit: Len is the first name of the thriller writer, so the surname completes him.

clue.text: I'm on an unrestricted diet and rove around on the other part of the bus

indicators.note: letters moved around end up in a different order
the other part of a longer word is what remains once the named portion is removed

parts.note: a bus was originally an omnibus; take away the bus and the other part is left
the letters of rove rearranged

explanation.surface: A passenger chatting about their diet while roving around the top deck of a bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places one piece after the other in this across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnivore eats both plants and meat, so its diet is unrestricted; the clue speaks in its voice.

clue.text: Said to be so different from say profound

parts.words: Said to be so different from say
parts.note: surface reading: something said to be unlike what one might say

parts.words: Said to be so different from say
parts.note: setter's reading: the verb forms said and say differ only in grammar, past against present

explanation.surface: A remark claimed to be quite unlike what one would usually say.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer splits as IN TENSE: said is past and say is present, so they differ in tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense feelings are deep and strong, so profound.

clue.text: Safe after a struggle to truss enemy up, relax

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the word is read from bottom to top
to truss is to tie up and enclose, so the outer letters bind the inner word
after a struggle things are knocked out of their order

parts.note: the letters of safe rearranged
a foe is an enemy

explanation.surface: Safe after a fight in which an enemy was tied up, someone can relax.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease off is to slacken effort, a phrasal synonym of relax.

clue.text: Messenger has some further messages

indicators.note: the phrase has some of the letters, a run tucked inside the words that follow

parts.note: taken from inside the two words

explanation.surface: A courier is carrying more letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Hermes was the messenger of the Greek gods, with winged sandals.

clue.text: Being in control brother finds a burden

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it

parts.note: to rein is to control, as with a horse
Fra is the title of an Italian friar, a brother

explanation.surface: A brother in charge finds responsibility heavy.
explanation.walkthrough: Burden suggests a load, but it also means the chorus of a song.
explanation.definitionFit: A burden in music is a repeated chorus, the same as a refrain.

clue.text: People separating to secure new significant others

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so the outer word grips the letter

parts.note: people who part are parters
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Couples splitting up while hoping to find new loves.
explanation.definitionFit: A significant other is a spouse or lover, which is what a partner is.

clue.text: Shot on the table in sanctuary

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in snooker, a defensive shot that leaves the opponent no easy pot

explanation.surface: A shot fired near a table in a place of refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: Shot suggests gunfire, but the table is a snooker table.
explanation.definitionFit: Sanctuary means protection from harm, the same as safety; in snooker a safety is a defensive shot.

clue.text: Riddle, special one, posed by reflective woman

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for special
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: a reflective name looks the same in a mirror, reading alike both ways

parts.note: Eve is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A special riddle set by a thoughtful woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Riddle sounds like a puzzle, but here it is the noun for a coarse sieve.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is a large coarse sieve for soil or gravel, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Start of the 26 taking most of the force

indicators.note: most of a word means it loses its final letter

parts.note: 26-across is a golf hole, and each hole starts at the tee
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something at the beginning absorbs most of a force.
explanation.definitionFit: A law with teeth has real force to make it effective, an idiom for power.

clue.text: Churchill heard noise from horse

indicators.note: heard means we go by what the ear takes in, not how a word is written

parts.note: a whinny is the high noise a horse makes

explanation.surface: Churchill hearing a horse whinny.
explanation.definitionFit: Winnie was the affectionate nickname of the wartime prime minister Winston Churchill.

clue.text: Starstruck old woman found a husband

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
Vera is a woman's name
a woman who found a husband wed

explanation.surface: An elderly lady is dazzled when she lands a husband.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone starstruck is dazzled into awe by a celebrity, so overawed fits.

clue.text: Part of course: all of it except the start

indicators.note: everything except the start means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: the whole is all of something

explanation.surface: Part of a course of study, all of it bar the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: Course suggests a lesson plan, but it is a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A golf course is divided into holes, usually eighteen of them.

clue.text: Theft punished with fine, far from the first

indicators.note: something punished is knocked about, so the letters are beaten into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A thief is punished by a fine for a first offence, or long after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Fifteenth place is well down the order, a long way from first.
